transcript.text: Hey, I'm Alex — this is a walkthrough of our mobile banking app, SwiftBank. We'll cover the core flows a developer would need to rebuild it.
This is the home dashboard. You can see the greeting, the checking account balance, and recent transactions, with a bottom navigation bar for the main sections.
I'm opening the Accounts tab, which lists all accounts with balances. Tapping the checking account opens its detail view.
The account detail screen shows a transaction list. Each row has a merchant name, a category, a date, and an amount.
Let me send some money. From the Payments tab I pick Send Money, choose a recipient, enter an amount, and continue.
On the review screen the app shows the amount, the recipient, and the fee — which is zero for standard transfers — before I confirm.
The success screen confirms the transfer with an animated check mark and a toast saying Money sent.
Next, the Cards tab. I'm freezing my debit card. The card flips to a frozen state with a badge, and unfreezing works the same way.
The transaction search filters by month and category. I'm selecting March, and the list updates to show only March transactions.
In settings, security lets you enable Face ID. The app asks to confirm your passcode before the toggle sticks.
For deposits, the app opens the camera and guides you through photographing the front and back of a check, then submits it for processing.
Bill pay lets you add a payee and schedule a payment. I'm adding City Power and Light and scheduling it for the first of the month.
The insights screen shows spending by category as a bar chart, with a monthly total at the top.
Dark mode is a one-tap toggle in settings. The whole interface switches theme instantly.
There's also a larger-text accessibility option, which scales the UI without breaking the layout.
Finally, signing out returns you to the sign-in screen with biometrics. That's the core of the app — thanks for watching.
I'm going to repeat the send flow with a second recipient so you can see it end to end.
Note the recent transactions update immediately after the transfer completes.
Let me switch between accounts — the app keeps the same tab structure for each one.
The card controls also include setting travel notices and adjusting limits.
For the last part, let me look at the insights breakdown again and compare the categories.
I'm switching back to light mode, and I'll leave it on the dashboard.

## Overview

A 12-minute screen recording of SwiftBank, a fictional mobile banking app, narrated by its designer. The recording covers the home dashboard, accounts, a send-money flow end to end, card freeze/unfreeze, transaction search, security settings, check deposit, bill pay, spending insights, dark mode, accessibility settings, and sign-out. ## Developer context

### Application
SwiftBank — a mobile banking app. Main areas: Home dashboard, Accounts, Payments (Send Money, Bill pay), Cards, Profile/Settings, Insights, and Deposit check. Sign-in uses passcode and Face ID (biometrics).

### UI hierarchy
- App shell: top header (screen title, back chevron on sub-screens) + bottom navigation (Home, Accounts, Payments, Cards, Profile)
- Home: greeting → checking balance card → recent transactions list
- Accounts: account cards → account detail (transaction list)
- Payments: Send Money (recipient → amount → review → success) · Bill pay (payees, schedule)
- Cards: card list → card controls (freeze, travel notice, limits)
- Settings: security (Face ID, passcode), appearance (dark mode, larger text)
- Insights: monthly total → category bar chart

### Navigation
Bottom tabs for the five main areas (observed). Sub-screens are pushed with a back chevron (observed). Transaction detail from a row tap is inferred (not shown in this recording).

### User interactions
- Select recipient from contact chips (observed)
- Enter amount; Continue enables when both fields are filled (observed)
- Confirm transfer → animated success + toast (observed)
- Freeze/unfreeze card via control; card artwork switches to grayscale (observed)
- Month chips filter transactions (observed)
- Face ID toggle requires passcode confirmation (observed)
- Check deposit via camera: front photo → back photo → submit → pending (observed)
- Bill pay: add payee, pick date, schedule (observed)
- Dark mode toggle applies instantly (observed)
- Larger text scales the UI (observed)
- Sign out returns to sign-in with biometrics (observed)

### Visible text inventory
- Home: "Good morning, Alex" · "Checking ····4821" · "$4,250.18" · "Recent transactions"
- Bottom nav: "Home" · "Accounts" · "Payments" · "Cards" · "Profile"

- Settings: "Dark mode" · "Larger text" · "Sign out" · "Sign in"

### Component relationships
- Bottom navigation persists across all main tabs (observed)
- The balance card pattern is shared by checking and savings (observed)
- Transaction rows: merchant, category chip, date, signed amount (observed)
- Success states replace the form screens rather than overlaying them (observed)
- The deposit amount appears derived from the check image (inferred)

### State transitions
- Send flow: form → review → processing → success → toast
- Card: active ⇄ frozen (grayscale + badge)
- Deposit: capture front → capture back → submit → pending
- Theme: light ⇄ dark (instant)
- Sign-in ⇄ app (after sign-out)

### Design patterns
- Rounded cards, ~16px gutters, single-column lists (observed)
- Large bold numerals for balances (observed)
- Category color-coding on the insights chart (uncertain)
- Toast notifications for confirmations (observed)

### Implementation-relevant observations
- The dashboard greeting uses the account holder's first name ("Good morning, Alex")
- Amounts use "$" formatting with two decimals; deposits show a "+" prefix
- The fee row displays "$0.00" for standard transfers (inferred as the default)
- Bottom navigation uses five items with icons and labels
- Passcode entry uses a numeric keypad sheet

### Uncertain items
- Chart colors per category
- Success-screen particle animation details
- Transaction-detail navigation behavior
